title: Strict-perfect local tensor model and relative Tor bounds on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with a conservative family of points (their stalk functors preserve finite limits and all small colimits and jointly detect isomorphisms). Let $R\to A$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and unbounded module derived categories with cochain localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor is computed using K-flat resolutions with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules with $M^q=0$ outside $[c,d]$, where $c\le d$ are integers, and assume its stalks are flat over the corresponding stalks of $R$ in every degree. Let $P\in D(A)$, let $U\in\mathcal C$, and suppose $P|_U\simeq Q(L^\bullet)$ on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$, where $L^p=0$ outside $[a,b]$, $a\le b$, and each $L^p$ is a direct summand of a finite free $A|_U$-module. Put $H=P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}Q(M^\bullet)$. There is an isomorphism in $D(A|_U)$ $$H|_U\simeq Q(T^\bullet),\qquad T^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet\otimes_{A|_U}M^\bullet|_U),$$ with signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Each $T^n$ is a finite direct sum of direct summands of finite direct sums of the $M^q|_U$, and $T^n=0$ for $n\notin[a+c,b+d]$. The scalar restriction of $T^\bullet$ is termwise flat and K-flat over $R|_U$. Scalar restriction identifies $H|_U$ with $Q(T^\bullet)$ also in $D(R|_U)$. For every $R$-module sheaf $F$, there is an isomorphism in $D(R|_U)$ $$(H\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F[0])|_U\simeq Q(T^\bullet\otimes_{R|_U}F|_U[0]),$$ whose cohomology vanishes outside $[a+c,b+d]$. No coherence, Noetherian, compactness, geometric morphism, or proper-support hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 0E8K (lemma-restriction-K-flat), 0DEN (lemma-check-K-flat-stalks); the local model calculation in spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0DKJ (lemma-tensor-perfect).

proof.text: Write $R_U=R|_U$, $A_U=A|_U$, and $M_U=M^\bullet|_U$. Apply the conservative-point flatness criterion to the underlying $R$-module of each $M^q$: its stalks are flat by hypothesis, so this is a flat $R$-module sheaf. Restriction of a flat sheaf to the slice is flat. Scalar restriction commutes with slice restriction because both retain the same underlying sections and compose their scalar actions with $R(V)\to A(V)$. Consequently each $M_U^q$, viewed over $R_U$, is flat.

Each $L^p$ is flat over $A_U$: tensoring with $A_U^{r_p}$ is the finite sum of $r_p$ identity functors, and tensoring with its direct summand $L^p$ is a direct summand of that exact functor. Exactness passes to a direct summand, since its kernels and images are the corresponding summands of the original kernels and images. Thus the definition of flatness applies. Since $L^p=0$ for $p>b$, the bounded-above flat-complex lemma makes $L^\bullet$ K-flat over $A_U$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); finite free local tensor calculation of spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0DKJ (lemma-tensor-perfect).

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat complex $K$ with $Q_AK\simeq P$, using the essential surjectivity in the K-flat localization equivalence. The one-sided tensor comparison gives $H\simeq Q_A\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_A M)$. Exact slice restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms, finite sums, and the cohomology of complexes. In any fixed total degree only the finitely many indices $c\le q\le d$ occur. Thus the ordinary sheaf tensor restriction isomorphisms, on the $(p,q)$ summands, give a chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_A M)|_U\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(K|_U\otimes_{A_U}M_U)$: naturality handles $d_K\otimes1$, $1\otimes d_M$, and the unchanged sign $(-1)^p$. The complex $K|_U$ remains K-flat and has flat terms by the two restriction lemmas. The one-sided comparison on the slice therefore identifies this localization with $P|_U\otimes_{A_U}^{\mathbf L}Q_{A_U}M_U$. This proves the restriction comparison needed here without requiring an unbounded direct sum to commute with restriction.

source.place: Tags 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 0E8K (lemma-restriction-K-flat); sites-modules.tex Tags 0E8J and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), localized-site case.

proof.text: Apply $-\otimes_{A_U}^{\mathbf L}Q_{A_U}M_U$ to the supplied isomorphism $P|_U\simeq Q_{A_U}L^\bullet$. Step 3 and the one-sided tensor comparison, now with the flat-term K-flat first factor $L^\bullet$ from step 2 and the arbitrary second factor $M_U$, give $H|_U\simeq Q_{A_U}L^\bullet\otimes_{A_U}^{\mathbf L}Q_{A_U}M_U\simeq Q_{A_U}\operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet\otimes_{A_U}M_U)$. This is the asserted $D(A_U)$ isomorphism and defines the specified complex $T$. No $A_U$-flatness of $M_U$ is used.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), including the preceding construction; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0DKJ (lemma-tensor-perfect), local tensor model.

proof.text: The definition of signed total tensor gives $T^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}L^p\otimes_{A_U}M_U^q$. Only pairs with $a\le p\le b$ and $c\le q\le d$ contribute, hence only finitely many. For a splitting $L^p\xrightarrow{i_p}A_U^{r_p}\xrightarrow{\pi_p}L^p$ with $\pi_pi_p=1$, tensoring the two maps with $M_U^q$ still has composite identity. The elementary finite-free tensor isomorphism $A_U^{r_p}\otimes_{A_U}M_U^q\simeq(M_U^q)^{r_p}$ sends $(z_j)\otimes m$ to $(z_jm)_j$, with inverse $(m_j)\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes m_j$ on sheafified generators. Thus each summand is a direct summand of a finite sum of $M_U^q$. If $n<a+c$ or $n>b+d$ there is no contributing pair and $T^n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DKJ (lemma-tensor-perfect), displayed local terms; sites-cohomology.tex tensor totalization construction before Tag 06YL.

proof.text: Regard step 5 over $R_U$. A finite sum of flat module sheaves is flat because tensoring an exact sequence with that sum gives the finite sum of its exact tensor sequences. A direct summand is flat: tensoring with its split inclusion and retraction makes the resulting sequence a direct summand of an exact sequence, and kernels and images split as in step 2. Step 1 says all $M_U^q$ are $R_U$-flat. Applying these two observations to the finite sum of summands in step 5 proves every scalar-restricted $T^n$ flat over $R_U$. This argument requires no flatness of $A_U$ over $R_U$.

source.place: Tag 0DKJ (lemma-tensor-perfect), last sentence on the relative Tor hypothesis; sites-modules.tex definition of flatness and finite direct-summand calculation.

proof.text: The scalar-restricted $T$ vanishes above $b+d$ and has flat $R_U$-terms by steps 5 and 6, so it is K-flat over $R_U$. The general scalar-restriction comparison says that termwise scalar restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $Q_{R_U}\operatorname{Res}(T)\simeq\operatorname{Res}(Q_{A_U}T)$. Apply that clause with its $B=A=R_U$, $S=A_U$, first ring map the identity and second ring map $R_U\to A_U$. Applying this functor to the $D(A_U)$ isomorphism of step 4 proves the asserted $D(R_U)$ identification. The termwise scalar and slice restrictions commute by their sectionwise definitions, so its left side is precisely the scalar restriction of $H|_U$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); sites-modules.tex change of rings section, restriction retains the underlying abelian sheaf.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $R$-module sheaf $F$, repeat the restriction calculation of step 3 over $R$, with the first derived object the scalar restriction of $H$ and the bounded second complex $F[0]$. Choose its first-factor representative from the K-flat localization equivalence; restriction preserves its flat terms and K-flatness, and now exactly one tensor summand occurs in each degree. This gives $(H\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F[0])|_U\simeq H|_U\otimes_{R_U}^{\mathbf L}F|_U[0]$. Substitute the $D(R_U)$ identification in step 7 and use the one-sided comparison with the flat-term K-flat complex $\operatorname{Res}(T)$. The result is $Q_{R_U}(T\otimes_{R_U}F|_U[0])$, with term $T^n\otimes_{R_U}F|_U$ and differential $d_T^n\otimes1$.

The complex in step 8 is zero in degree $n$ whenever $n<a+c$ or $n>b+d$, by step 5 and $0\otimes F|_U=0$. Its cohomology in such a degree is the quotient of a subobject of the zero degree-$n$ term, hence is zero. The derived isomorphism in step 8 carries this cohomology vanishing to the left side. All constructions also apply to zero complexes, rank-zero summands, a degenerate one-degree interval, and an empty slice.
